claims.how: The value 0.5 is the honeybee lateral ocellus figure from R9; the compound eye records give 0.25 to 0.53, so this is taken at the top of the range.
The records give 200, 270, 300 and 312 degrees; 240 is a middle choice within that spread, so it is invented and graded g.

quotes.quote: They found that the highest spatial frequency reliably resolved by the bees was 0.26 cycle deg−1, with no evidence of a difference in acuity between horizontal and vertical gratings.
The orientation of the gratings can be clearly observed even with 2° patterns and the imaged gratings are quite sharp.
The spatial resolving power of the two species did not differ (A. australis: 0.53 ± 0.03 cpd; mean ± SEM; T. carbonaria: 0.53 ± 0.02; Fig. 3b; Table 1
Seidl and Kaiser (1981) reported that the honeybee FOV extends down to −90° in elevation and back to −156° in azimuth (at 0° el.)
collects a composite image of the panorama in radial coordinates over about 200° horizontally
Bees can see ~300° horizontally on the body plane with low spatial resolution for peripheral ommatidia
a very coarse representation of the whole 270° bee eye horizontal field of view
